entries.clue: A horse and sheep mixed up word (7)

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse
a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: A farmyard jumble of a horse and a sheep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mixed up' looks like an instruction to rearrange letters, but it belongs to the definition: an anagram is literally a mixed-up word.
annotation.definitionFit: An anagram is a word whose letters have been rearranged.

entries.clue: Call upon old man to return ring (6)

indicators.note: returning sends PA back the way it came, giving AP

blocks.note: a peal is a ring of bells

annotation.surface: Visiting an elderly father and asking him to give a ring back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is a colloquial term for one's father, so PA; 'ring' is the sound of bells, not jewellery.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you call upon a court or a friend when you ask them for a decision or help.

entries.clue: Advanced convenience for reps (6)

blocks.note: a convenience is a public toilet; the Gents is the men's one

annotation.surface: A modern toilet facility laid on for sales representatives.
annotation.walkthrough: In British English a 'convenience' (public convenience) is a public toilet, and 'the Gents' is the men's toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Sales reps act as agents for the firms whose goods they sell.

entries.clue: Controlled remainder getting showered (10)

annotation.surface: Whatever was left over got a soaking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is only a link, and 'Controlled' is an adjective here, as in a restrained, controlled manner.
annotation.definitionFit: Restrained behaviour is controlled, kept in check.

entries.clue: Bloke A consumes new, delicious food (5)

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so MAN A swallows N

annotation.surface: A man tucking into some newly made tasty food.
annotation.walkthrough: N slips between MAN and A. 'Bloke' is everyday British slang for a man.
annotation.definitionFit: Manna, the food from heaven, is used of anything delightful to eat.

entries.clue: Obedient don upset the irritable female urology lecturer initially (7)

indicators.note: take each word at its start: its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: don upset the irritable female urology lecturer
blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these seven words

annotation.surface: An upset academic and a tetchy urology lecturer, with the don described as obedient.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'don' is an Oxford or Cambridge lecturer, which suits the university scene, but here it only lends its D.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone dutiful does what is asked of them, so is obedient.

entries.clue: Rash individual read about was raised (9)

indicators.note: turned about, READ's letters are rearranged
in a down entry, raising LIVED lifts it so it reads bottom to top

annotation.surface: A reckless person who was brought up hearing about something they read.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was raised' looks like upbringing; instead 'was' becomes LIVED and 'raised' flips it upward in this down answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless person who takes rash risks.

entries.clue: Toiletry regularly causing row (4)

indicators.note: at regular intervals: every other letter

annotation.surface: A bathroom product that keeps starting arguments.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel in the surface, but the answer takes its other sense: a line, as in a tier of seats.
annotation.definitionFit: A tier is one row in a stacked series, like seats in a stadium.

entries.clue: Loud atmosphere by quiet place for justice (4,4)

blocks.note: to lay something down is to place it

annotation.surface: A noisy atmosphere next to a quiet spot set aside for justice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loud' and 'quiet' are the musical markings f and p; 'place' is a verb, to lay.
annotation.definitionFit: Fair play is just, even-handed treatment.

entries.clue: Paid attention as told stories about revolutionary traps (8)

indicators.note: LIED goes about, around, the next part
revolving sends NETS round the other way: STEN

blocks.note: to tell stories is to lie
nets catch things, as traps do

annotation.surface: Someone lying about a revolutionary's traps while others paid attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Told stories' is the euphemism for fibbing, and 'revolutionary' here is a turn, not a rebel.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense, matching 'paid'.

entries.clue: Decrease pressure concerning steam ship? (5)

annotation.surface: A worry about reducing the pressure in a steamship's boiler.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: read 'Decrease' as de-crease, to take the creases out, which is what pressing clothes does.
annotation.definitionFit: Pressing with an iron takes the creases out, so 'de-creases' the fabric.

entries.clue: Manage flipping cycle to garden centres (9)

indicators.note: flipping RUN over turns it back to front: NUR

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
a cycle of songs or plays is a series

annotation.surface: Trying to manage the wretched bike ride out to the garden centre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British curse word, but it is doing the reversing; 'cycle' is a series, not a bike.
annotation.definitionFit: Nurseries are places where plants are raised and sold, i.e. garden centres.

entries.clue: Dessert going around hospital room later (10)

indicators.note: AFTERS goes around WARD, enclosing it

blocks.note: afters is British slang for pudding
a ward is a room of beds in a hospital

annotation.surface: Pudding being wheeled around a hospital ward to be eaten later.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain 'afters' is a casual word for dessert, the course that comes after the main one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adverbs place an event after the present one.

entries.clue: Slip left out in part of church (4)

indicators.note: left goes out: L is removed

blocks.note: a lapse is a slip or error

annotation.surface: A slip made while leaving part of a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left out' reads as omitted, which is roughly the instruction, but it splits: 'left' is L and 'out' does the removing.
annotation.definitionFit: The apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church.

entries.clue: Kelvin and Nicholas with skill to make trifle (5-5)

blocks.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin

annotation.surface: Two men, Kelvin and Nicholas, deftly making a trifle for pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'trifle' the layered British pudding; the answer takes its other sense, a small worthless ornament.
annotation.definitionFit: A knick-knack is a trifle: a small ornament of little value.

entries.clue: Dads navigate strangely unfavourable circumstance (12)

indicators.note: arranged strangely: the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Fathers getting lost as they find their way, to their cost.
annotation.walkthrough: A fitting surface: dads navigating strangely is a family road-trip cliche, and all twelve letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary-style gloss: a handicap or drawback that works against you.

entries.clue: Claim senorita’s wrong (9)

indicators.note: put together wrongly: the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters, the apostrophe ignored

annotation.surface: Saying that a young Spanish woman has got it wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive's S counts as a letter; punctuation is ignored in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are nouns for something stated as true.

entries.clue: Home of upwardly mobile blue fish (8)

indicators.note: moving upward in a down entry, LEWD reads bottom to top

blocks.note: the ling is a sea fish

annotation.surface: The house of a socially ambitious, sad fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' suggests social climbing but just means 'moving up' in this down entry; 'blue' means risqué, not sad.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the formal word estate agents and officials use for a house.

entries.clue: Sketch of gent I’ve developed over time (8)

indicators.note: developed into something else: the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An artist's portrait of a gentleman, worked up over a long period.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' only tells you T sits with the fodder; all eight letters are mixed together.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short written or drawn portrait of a scene or character.

entries.clue: Servers right to replace a plug for author’s unfortunate condition (7,5)

indicators.note: R takes the place of the A in WAITERS

blocks.note: R = right, swapped in for A
to plug a hole is to block it

annotation.surface: Restaurant staff unplug something that ruins a novelist's day.
annotation.walkthrough: The swap WAITERS to WRITERS is the key step; the definition is the author's inability to write.
annotation.definitionFit: Writer's block is an author's unfortunate inability to produce new work.

entries.clue: Win over upset artists in poorly lit surroundings (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting RAS turns it upside down: SAR
SAR sits in DIM's surroundings

annotation.surface: Winning over some disgruntled artists in a gloomy studio.
annotation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: charm takes away someone's hostility, as if taking their weapons.

entries.clue: Ran wearing sash (6)

blocks.note: to belt along is to run fast
wearing a belt or sash around the waist

annotation.surface: Someone running in a sash, like a pageant contestant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Belted' for sprinting is informal British usage: 'he belted down the road'.
annotation.definitionFit: Belted means ran very fast, and also fitted with a belt or sash.

entries.clue: Roll ankle somewhat and limp (4)

indicators.note: only some of the words: part of them holds the answer

blocks.note: the answer spans the end of 'Roll' and the start of 'ankle'

annotation.surface: Twisting an ankle a bit and hobbling off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Limp' is a verb in the surface (to hobble) but an adjective in the answer: lank hair is limp.
annotation.definitionFit: Lank hair hangs limp and lifeless.

entries.clue: Fined baker juggling sharp object (5,5)

indicators.note: juggled letters are tossed around and rearranged

annotation.surface: A baker penalised for juggling a knife.
annotation.walkthrough: Nicely apt: the fodder mentions a baker, and the answer is a baker's tool, the very thing being juggled.
annotation.definitionFit: A bread knife is a sharp object used for slicing loaves.

entries.clue: Abolish article by new union leader at first (5)

indicators.note: the leader's first letter

annotation.surface: Scrapping a piece written by the new head of a trade union.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Union leader' tempts you to take U alone, but 'leader at first' is its own piece: L.
annotation.definitionFit: To annul a law or marriage is to abolish it, declaring it void.

entries.clue: Fellow I will satisfy (4)

annotation.surface: A man promising that he will please.
annotation.walkthrough: Crosswords ignore apostrophes, so I'LL goes in as ILL.
annotation.definitionFit: To fill a need is to satisfy it; eating your fill satisfies hunger.

entries.clue: Gut feeling during instruction (9)

blocks.note: in = during, as in 'in the night'

annotation.surface: Having a hunch in the middle of a lesson.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gut feeling during instruction' reads as a hunch in class, but 'during' is just the two-letter preposition that opens the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Intuition is a gut feeling, knowing without reasoning.

entries.clue: Separate acting role (5)

blocks.note: an actor is given one role, one part, in a play

annotation.surface: A role distinct from the rest of the cast.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense needs a split in the letters: read the answer as two words, the article plus the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: 'living separate' means living apart, and an acting role is a part.

entries.clue: Smile about European male oddly finding mischievous spirit (7)

indicators.note: GRIN goes about, around, the other letters
the odd-numbered letters: M and L of MaLe

blocks.note: a grin is a broad smile

annotation.surface: Grinning at a strange European man who turns out to be an imp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'strangely' but here it means the odd letters: M(a)L(e).
annotation.definitionFit: A gremlin is a mischievous imaginary sprite blamed for mechanical faults.

entries.clue: Left one king and noble woman spinning furiously (4,3)

indicators.note: spinning turns DAME round: EMAD

blocks.note: a dame is a woman with a title equivalent to a knighthood

annotation.surface: A king and a titled lady left alone, dancing wildly.
annotation.walkthrough: A Dame is the female counterpart of a knight in the British honours system.
annotation.definitionFit: To do something like mad is to do it furiously, with frantic energy.
